read.sections.2.text.note: Added '(kopi)' after the English word 'coffee' so learners know the word; the rest of the etymology is unchanged. Persian = 'bahasa Persia'. Indonesian 'kopi' also comes from Arabic (via Dutch), which teachers might like to mention, but I did not add it.
read.sections.2.text.back: Languages change over time. Languages also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word "coffee" (kopi) has travelled a long way. At first, it was the Arabic word qahwah. Then it became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, until finally it came into English. Many languages are also related to each other. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one language family, because all three grew from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another language. Every language carries knowledge and stories from the people who use it.
read.sections.2.text.source: Languages change over time. They also borrow words from each other when people meet and trade. The English word “coffee” travelled a long way. It started as the Arabic word qahwah. It became kahveh in Turkish and caffè in Italian, and then it reached English. Many languages are also related. English, Hindi and Persian belong to one language family, because they grew from one very old language. Arabic, Somali and Hausa belong to another family. No language is better than another. Each one carries the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it.

read.sections.1.text.note: Deaf = 'Tuli' with a capital T, as Indonesian Deaf organisations write it. United Nations = 'Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa (PBB)'.
read.sections.1.text.back: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign languages, which are complete languages with their own grammar. The United Nations (UN) says there are more than 300 sign languages in the world. People also use body movements, pictures and clear design. The pictograms on the notice show food, a clock, a calendar and a map. This makes the notice more accessible, because more people can understand its main message. But pictures cannot give every detail, for example what needs to be brought. A volunteer who can translate still helps.
read.sections.1.text.source: Communication is not only speaking and writing. Deaf communities use sign languages, which are full languages with their own grammar. The United Nations says there are more than 300 sign languages in the world. People also use gestures, pictures and clear design. The pictogram on the notice shows food, a clock, a calendar and a map. This makes the notice more accessible, because more people can understand the main message. But a picture cannot give every detail, such as what to bring. A volunteer who can interpret still helps.

read.sections.0.text.note: Malay = 'bahasa Melayu'. 'Speaking more than one language is a strength' (learningGoal) = 'sebuah kelebihan'.
read.sections.0.text.back: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and care. Hearing words you know can make you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual. In Paraguay, for example, many people speak Spanish and Guaraní. People who can speak Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. How fluently someone speaks English does not show how smart they are. It also does not show whether their ideas are important or not.
read.sections.0.text.source: People use language to share news, jokes, memories and care. Hearing a word you know can help you feel welcome in a new place. Many people in the world are multilingual. In Paraguay, for example, many people speak both Spanish and Guaraní. Someone who speaks Somali, Arabic and English, or Tamil and Malay, can help different groups understand each other. That is a real skill. How well a person speaks English does not show how clever they are. It does not show whether their ideas matter.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Languages change over time. Languages take words from each other. Look at the word "coffee" (kopi). It came from Arabic. Then it went into Turkish and Italian. After that it went into English. Some languages are like cousins. Those languages grew from one old language. So they are in one language family. English, Hindi and Persian are in one family. Arabic, Somali and Hausa are in another family. No language is the best. Every language holds the stories of the people who use it.

write.example.back: I would add notices in two or three languages that the visitors use. This helps because more people can read it in a language they know. I would also place a helper who can translate at the door. This helps people ask questions, for example what they need to bring. One weakness is that a written notice cannot help people who cannot read. The pictures and the helper can help with that. This shows that using more than one way to get a message across helps more people feel welcome.

watch.summary.back: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke one language spread out. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed the way they spoke. New words came in, and sounds changed. Over time, one language became several languages. Languages that grew from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, like numbers, to find these links. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so the experts check them carefully. Sometimes it is hard to say where one language ends and another begins. Because of that, different experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with an idea: a language that sounds new to you might be related to a language you know.
watch.summary.source: This animated video explains how languages change. Long ago, groups of people who spoke one language moved apart. They lived in new places and met new neighbours. Over many years, each group changed the way it spoke. New words came in, and sounds changed. In time, one language became several languages. Languages that grew from one older language form a language family. Language experts compare grammar and basic words, like numbers, to find these links. Some words are borrowed from neighbours, so experts check them with care. It can be hard to say where one language ends and another begins. So different experts count between 3,000 and 8,000 languages in the world. The video ends with an idea: a language that sounds new to you may be related to one you know.
